title: Ranji Trophy: Bengal lead Maharashtra by one run with six wickets left going into final day
dek: Rain cut day three at Eden Gardens to 27.5 overs. Shami finished with four wickets as Maharashtra took a 75-run first-innings lead, and Bengal closed on 76 for 4.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bengal will start the last day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match against Maharashtra at Eden Gardens on Thursday on 76 for 4 in their second innings, just one run ahead. Rain and bad light restricted Wednesday's third day to 27.5 overs, RevSportz reported.

The first session was washed out. When play began, Mohammed Shami ended the 70-ball resistance of Maharashtra's No. 11, Pradeep Dadhe, to finish with 4 for 37. Maharashtra were all out for 218, a first-innings lead of 75 over Bengal's 143. Tanay Sanghavi, in only his third first-class match, was left unbeaten on 60.

Bengal then slid to three wickets for 25. Captain Abhimanyu Easwaran, Sudip Gharami and Sudip Chatterjee all fell cheaply. Ankur Paul made 32 and added 49 for the fourth wicket with Abhishek Porel before he was out to Hitesh Walunj. Porel was 23 not out at stumps, with Suraj Jaiswal alongside him.

Bengal are unbeaten in the competition this season. With overcast weather forecast again, the first session on Thursday will decide whether they can bat out the draw or whether Maharashtra get a chance to push for an outright win. If the match is drawn, Maharashtra get the first-innings points.
